clue.text: Knows I'm an embarrassing member of the family

indicators.note: something embarrassing throws one into confusion, so these letters are put into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to knowing a relative who causes them shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embarrassing' looks like it describes the relative, but it tells you to rearrange KNOWS, IM and AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A female relative is a member of one's family by blood or marriage.

clue.text: Neckcloth appears when hand is taken from tissue

indicators.note: these words say one piece is removed from the other

parts.note: a tissue is a paper hanky, a cloth for the nose
taken as written

explanation.surface: A neckerchief turns up when a hand is removed from a tissue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is taken from' removes the word HAND from the front of the longer word for a tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: A square of cloth worn round the neck or over the head.

clue.text: Four different points thrown into TV bulletin

parts.note: the four compass points north, east, west, south
cast means thrown

explanation.surface: Four separate points get worked into a television news item.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast of the news on radio or television.

clue.text: Create by slow degrees and do the trick at university

parts.note: to work is to succeed or do the trick
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student slowly prepares a conjuring routine at college.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you are 'up' at university when in residence.
explanation.definitionFit: To develop or build something gradually, as one builds an appetite.

clue.text: Very small fly on shirt

parts.note: a midge is a small fly
T as in T-shirt

explanation.surface: A tiny insect lands on someone's shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the fly above the shirt letter.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means miniature or tiny.

clue.text: What might be left in fire after 5th of month

definitions.text: What might be left in fire after 5th of month

parts.words: What might be left in fire after 5th of month
parts.note: a bonfire on the fifth leaves part of the month still to come, the remainder of the eleventh month

explanation.surface: Ashes or embers remaining after a bonfire night.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonfire Night, 5 November, is when British bonfires burn Guy Fawkes effigies; what is 'left' is the rest of the month.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh month, whose fifth day is Bonfire Night in Britain.

clue.text: Something afoot for church musician

parts.note: read literally: a lever worked by the foot, which an organist in church uses for the bass notes

explanation.surface: Something is brewing for the church organist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afoot' usually means 'under way', but here it means literally operated by the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ has a keyboard for the feet, each lever played by the organist's foot.

clue.text: Not causing suffering when father is out more presumably

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
someone out more often is in less

explanation.surface: Life is easier when Dad spends more time away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as father 'in less', i.e. out more; 'presumably' admits the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Free from hurt or distress, causing no ache.

clue.text: Dorothy has a way with one showing excessive fondness

parts.note: Dot is a short form of Dorothy
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Dorothy has her own approach to someone besotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dotes, doting through foolish affection or senility.

clue.text: Going in front for the most part during introduction

indicators.note: only most of the word is used, losing its final letter

parts.note: going in front is leading

explanation.surface: Being ahead for most of the time during an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A preamble or opening passage that leads into the main matter.

clue.text: Some of the crew I rediscovered had provided new cables

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a crew finds something again and fits fresh wiring.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit a building with new electrical wiring is to give it new cables.

clue.text: Emerald isle?

parts.note: not Ireland, as the phrase suggests, but an island whose name literally describes a green country

explanation.surface: A poetic name for Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emerald Isle' is a standard nickname for Ireland; the question mark invites a literal reading of an island named for its colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The huge Arctic island is called after a verdant colour, matching 'emerald' as a shade of green.

clue.text: Having trouble travelling to Spain

indicators.note: letters that travel move about, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tourist experiences difficulties on the road to Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being in difficulty or a predicament.

clue.text: Mr or Mrs north?

parts.note: Brenda is a woman's name, so a married lady could be Mrs Brenda

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about which title to use for someone from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Adding N to a woman's name gives a man's name, so the clue plays the two titles against each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name, so its bearer could be addressed as a mister.

clue.text: Present day figure

parts.note: not a modern personality but the figure associated with the day of presents, 25 December

explanation.surface: A contemporary celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present day' suggests 'modern'; read it as the day for gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Claus, the bringer of gifts, is the figurehead of the gift-giving day in December.

clue.text: One investigating pioneer?

definitions.meaning: someone who travels to unknown places first

explanation.surface: A researcher who breaks new ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a person who examines something closely and one who journeys into uncharted territory.

clue.text: Verify total using computer system

parts.note: to check is to verify
a sum is a total

explanation.surface: Confirm the final figure using computing.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit-count value used in computing to detect errors in transmitted data.

clue.text: Object of terror on ear of maize is pest in the hothouse

indicators.note: on here means attached to, so one piece is added to the other

parts.note: mealie (also spelt mealy) is South African for an ear of maize
bug is an old word for a bogey or object of terror, as in bugbear

explanation.surface: A frightening creature on a corncob is a greenhouse nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are rare: 'bug' meaning bogey survives in bugbear, and 'mealie' is South African for maize.
explanation.definitionFit: A sap-sucking insect with a white waxy coat, a common glasshouse plant pest.

clue.text: Second mentioned of two in partnership is a floozie

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the partnership letters

parts.note: North and South are partners in bridge, giving S and N
the latter is the second of two things named

explanation.surface: In a business partnership the junior partner turns out to be a loose woman.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South play as partners, so 'partnership' gives S and N around LATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a slovenly or promiscuous woman, a slut.

clue.text: Difficulty having little weight

definitions.meaning: an old apothecaries' unit of twenty grains

explanation.surface: A problem involving something light.
explanation.definitionFit: A qualm that holds one back from acting, and also a tiny apothecaries' measure of weight.

clue.text: Bird is in hide

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: hide is animal skin

explanation.surface: A bird sits in a birdwatcher's shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' suggests a birdwatching shelter, but it is the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A small yellow-green finch.

clue.text: Beat blues afterwards

parts.note: a word for beat which is followed by blues in the name of a music genre, R and B

explanation.surface: Defeat depression later.
explanation.walkthrough: The genre 'rhythm and blues' puts blues after this word for beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular pattern of beats in music.

clue.text: Many an article has been cut short by artist on Greek instrument

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
an article is a thing, which can be called it

indicators.note: the word has loses its final letter

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist

explanation.surface: Lots of objects were trimmed by a painter working on an ancient lyre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'been cut short' removes the S from HAS to leave HA.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient lyre-like stringed instrument played by the Greeks.

clue.text: Business takes abstainer on to produce thread

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
TT means teetotal, one who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: A firm hires a teetotaller to make yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: Spun fibre from the cotton plant used for sewing.

clue.text: The first believer

parts.note: taken as written
1st, with I for 1, is first

explanation.surface: The original man of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: One who believes in a god.

clue.text: Send up salad plant, shoot up very fast

parts.note: to sky a ball is to hit it high into the air
rocket is a peppery salad leaf, called arugula in the US

explanation.surface: A gardener hurls a salad leaf high in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices or values that rise steeply are said to shoot upward like a firework.

clue.text: It is sought by game hunters — usually indoors!

definitions.text: It is sought by game hunters — usually indoors!

parts.words: It is sought by game hunters — usually indoors!
parts.note: not shooting game but a parlour game in which players hunt for a small hidden sewing object

explanation.surface: A quarry pursued by sportsmen, oddly inside the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game hunters' suggests shooting; the game is the children's party game hunt the thimble.
explanation.definitionFit: The finger guard used in sewing is the item hidden in a traditional party game.

clue.text: Most of manure removed from place in Belgium!

indicators.note: the remaining letters are moved around into a new order
most of the word means all but its last letter

explanation.surface: Dung cleared away from a Belgian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the final E of MANURE; 'removed' then rearranges MANUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A city and province in Wallonia, southern Belgium.

clue.text: Timely shooter?

parts.note: a firearm that keeps time, fired at intervals of sixty seconds

explanation.surface: A gunman with good timing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannon fired once every sixty seconds, as a signal of distress or mourning.
